status.scope_reason: The company provides comprehensive commercial drone-as-a-service (DaaS) operations, including agricultural spraying, mapping, and industrial inspection, using its own manufactured drone fleet.
status.evidence: An October 2026 report by VCCircle notes that Garuda Aerospace Ltd has completed its pre-IPO funding round and actively provides Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) solutions alongside drone manufacturing.

claims.claim: The company reports operating a fleet of more than 400 drones and 500 pilots across 84 cities, manufacturing 30 types of drones, including its flagship camera drone Droni, agricultural Kisan drones, and the Trishul border patrol surveillance drone.
claims.source: https://thehindu.com, https://dronelife.com/2024/01/31/garuda-aerospace-introduces-droni-indias-smart-personal-drone-in-consumer-photography-and-cinematography/, https://www.garudaaerospace.com/products/defense-drones/trishul

claims.claim: The company announced in March 2026 that it is expanding its fleet with Airbus Helicopters' Flexrotor platform to deliver long-endurance aerial intelligence for energy, infrastructure, agriculture, and defense applications.
claims.source: https://airbus.com

claims.claim: The company reports it was granted 20 patents (including six international patents) covering agricultural solutions like mapping, spraying, crop health monitoring, and field surveillance, as well as underwater inspection and miniature radar system drones.
claims.source: https://economictimes.com

claims.claim: The company reports offering extensive Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) solutions spanning precision agriculture (precision spraying, crop health monitoring, and soil mapping), industrial operations (structural, pipeline, boiler, and solar panel inspections), asset tracking, 2D/3D photogrammetry mapping, LiDAR surveying, bathymetric surveys, and tactical defense surveillance.
claims.source: https://www.garudaaerospace.com/

claims.claim: The company reports utilizing high-resolution imaging and real-time analytics for strategic decision-making across enterprise operations, and it deployed the AgriQ Engine in August 2026 as an AI-powered crop health monitoring platform to provide data-driven field intelligence for farmers.
claims.note: deployment date of August 2026 as a newly introduced engine
claims.source: https://x.com/garuda_india/status/2092192702742102218, https://www.instagram.com/p/DFIOt0CtCaC/

claims.claim: The company entered a strategic collaboration with Salesforce in December 2025 to integrate cloud-first tools including Agentforce AI algorithms to deliver real-time actionable insights and eliminate client data silos across its workflows.
claims.corrected: The company entered a strategic collaboration with Salesforce in December 2025 to integrate cloud-first tools including Agentforce AI algorithms to deliver real-time actionable insights and eliminate client data silos across its workflows.
claims.source: https://www.salesforce.com/in/news/press-releases/2025/12/23/garuda-aerospace-adopts-salesforce-agentforce/

claims.claim: The company has obtained a total of six DGCA approvals, including a Type Certificate for its small category "GA-AD" Kisan drone in December 2022, a Type Certificate for medium category drones in November 2023, and a Delta-type certification for small drone manufacturing in October 2024.
claims.corrected: The company has obtained a total of six DGCA approvals, including a Type Certificate for its small category "GA-AG" Kisan drone in December 2022, a Type Certificate for medium category drones in November 2023, and a Delta-type certification for small drone manufacturing in October 2024.
claims.source: https://aviationworld.in/garuda-aerospace-doubles-down-with-dgca-approval-for-manufacturing-and-training/ and https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/aviation/garuda-aerospace-receives-type-certification-and-rtpo-approvals-from-dgca/96505671

claims.claim: The company secured Remote Pilot Training Organisation (RPTO) authorization from the DGCA for small and medium class drones and received a Train the Trainer approval in October 2024.
claims.source: https://aviationworld.in/garuda-aerospace-doubles-down-with-dgca-approval-for-manufacturing-and-training/ and https://www.thehindu.com/business/garuda-aerospace-bags-medium-class-rpto-authorisation-from-dgca/article67706834.ece

claims.claim: Garuda Aerospace announced in July 2025 that it secured multiple high-value contracts from various government departments in Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Jharkhand, including the Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Limited, Central Mine Planning & Design Institute, and Jharkhand Exploration and Mining Corporation Limited, to provide drone-based survey and monitoring services across mine leases.
claims.source: https://m.economictimes.com/news/defence/garuda-aerospace-bags-contracts-from-state-govts-for-ai-powered-drone-solutions/articleshow/122228038.cms

claims.claim: The company was awarded a formal work contract by Rajasthan Electronics & Instruments Limited in March 2026 to establish and operate a DGCA-authorised Remote Pilot Training Organisation in Jaipur.
claims.source: https://www.deccanherald.com/india/rajasthan/garuda-aerospace-partners-with-reil-expands-national-drone-skill-3942788

claims.claim: According to audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026, Garuda Aerospace Limited recorded a 66.8% year-over-year increase in revenue from operations to ₹205.96 crore and a 41.1% growth in net profit after tax to ₹25.92 crore.
claims.source: Garuda Aerospace Standalone Audited Accounts / Financial Reports via UnlistedValley and UnlistedArena (September/October 2026)

claims.claim: The company secured $10 million (approximately ₹96 crore) in a pre-IPO funding round in October 2026 at a pre-money valuation of $320 million, with participation from the Motherson family office and Aditum Investment Group.
claims.source: The Economic Times and Pre-IPO funding announcements (October 2026)

claims.claim: The company reports a widespread geographical reach spanning 84 cities across India, supported by a network of over 500 pilots and an operational presence across multiple states.
claims.source: Garuda Aerospace corporate declarations, official media announcements, and DRHP filings (2025-2026)

claims.claim: The company announced a strategic partnership with Redington Limited in February 2026 to drive national go-to-market, enterprise sales, channel enablement, and service support for its indigenous drone solutions across India.
claims.source: Garuda Aerospace and Redington Limited official joint partnership press releases (February 2026)

claims.claim: The company signed a strategic alliance agreement with Airbus in 2026 to expand the deployment of the Airbus Flexrotor unmanned aerial systems through a Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model, and signed an MoU with Thales in July 2024 to promote safe and secure drone operations in India.
claims.source: Airbus official press releases (March 2026) and Thales-Garuda Aerospace MoU announcements (July/August 2024)

claims.claim: The company reports having a vast network that includes 4,000 pilots across 400 districts in India as of March 2026.
claims.note: The network details of 4,000 pilots across 400 districts as of March 2026 are unconfirmed. Records mention over 4,000 drones and 4,000+ trained pilots across 80+ cities in March 2026, or 500 pilots across 84 cities in FY25, but do not state the 400 districts metric for this date.
claims.source: UnlistedZone Research, Minton, The CEO Magazine

claims.claim: The company reports that its fleet of over 2,000 agricultural drones achieved one million flight hours in a single year, operating at a continuous rate of one deployment every two minutes, and its cumulative operations reached over 1.2 million flight hours by August 2026.
claims.source: Economic Times, Garuda Aerospace Ltd Facebook Page/Official Video updates

status.scope_reason: The company directly operates drone-based agricultural chemical spraying services for external clients under the AgriWings brand.
status.evidence: According to the official AgriWings company profile, the brand operates as an agricultural drone spraying service provided by D2F Services Private Limited.

claims.claim: The company reports a total fleet size of over 100 drones, having deployed 60% of this total fleet for spraying operations across multiple states.
claims.source: The Hindu BusinessLine (https://thehindubusinessline.com) and BioVoice News (https://biovoicenews.com)

claims.claim: The company reported the deployment of its D2F AI Farm project in partnership with Triveni Sugar Mill, which uses drones and IoT sensors to collect field data for crop health and disease-risk analysis powered by the CropGain OS and AI/ML models.
claims.corrected: The company reported the deployment of its D2F AI Farm project in partnership with Triveni Sugar Mill, which uses drones and IoT sensors to collect field data for crop health and disease-risk analysis.
claims.note: The feature involving CropGain OS and its integrated AI/ML models belongs to a completely separate company named CropGain, not AgriWings.
claims.source: LinkedIn Official Company Posts (https://linkedin.com and https://www.linkedin.com/posts/arsh-frutri_cropgain-cropgainos-cgdrone-activity-7506183773580038144-LdOe)

claims.claim: The company reports providing its Village Level Entrepreneur channel and independent operators with Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) certification, government subsidies, and structured training.
claims.source: AgriWings Official Website (https://agriwings.in/) and Agriculture Post (https://agriculturepost.com)

claims.claim: The company's hiring requirements specify that field operators must possess a valid DGCA license or Remote Pilot Certificate for drone operations.
claims.source: AgriWings Official Job Postings and Guidelines on Instagram (https://instagram.com) and LinkedIn (https://linkedin.com)

claims.claim: The company reported plans to expand drone-based spraying services to 1.5 lakh acres in the 2024 season, having sprayed over 20,000 acres for more than 2,500 farmers in the previous season across Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.
claims.source: The Hindu BusinessLine (https://thehindubusinessline.com) and FNB News (https://fnbnews.com)

claims.claim: The company announced a strategic corporate partnership with ADAMA India to demonstrate efficient drone spraying technology in apple orchards in Solan, Himachal Pradesh.
claims.source: LinkedIn post by AgriWings ("AgriWings partnered with ADAMA India to demonstrate efficient drone spraying technology in an apple orchard in Solan, Himachal Pradesh")

claims.claim: D2F Services Pvt. Ltd, operating under the brand AgriWings, won an agricultural drone service contract valued at ₹8.27 lakh from the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare in March 2023.
claims.corrected: Vista AgriWings won an agricultural drone service contract valued at ₹8.27 lakh from the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare in March 2023.
claims.source: Tenderkart award data for Tender Ref GEM/2023/B/3061825 (L1 Bidder Name listed as Vista AgriWings, not D2F Services Pvt. Ltd)

claims.claim: The company announced plans to scale up its operations to spray 1.5 lakh acres of land during the 2024 season, following a deployment of over 20,000 acres in the previous season.
claims.source: The Hindu BusinessLine ("AgriWings plans to spray 1.5 lakh acres this season. The company had sprayed in more than 20,000 acres in the previous season")

claims.claim: The company announced its commercial expansion into South India, specifically establishing agricultural drone spraying operations in selected regions of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
claims.source: Startagist and Food Infotech media reports ("AgriWings... has announced its expansion into the southern states of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka")

claims.claim: The company reports a collaboration with corporate partner Syngenta India to showcase drone technology in agriculture at the Farmer Mela in Kartarpur, Punjab, in September 2024.
claims.source: AgriWings official Instagram publication from September 2024 ("AgriWings, in collaboration with our corporate partner Syngenta India, proudly showcased the power of drone technology in agriculture at the Farmer Mela in Kartarpur, Punjab")

claims.claim: The company reports a collaboration with Corteva Agriscience to conduct its first farmer engagement event and run a 2026 maize drone-spray program in Bihar.
claims.corrected: The company reports a collaboration with Corteva Agriscience to conduct its first farmer engagement event and run a 2024–25 maize drone-spray program in Bihar.
claims.source: LinkedIn Post (January 2026), AgriWings x Corteva Agriscience Case Study (February 2026)

claims.claim: The company reported in June 2024 that it deployed 60 percent of a fleet consisting of over 100 drones for agricultural spraying services.
claims.source: The Hindu BusinessLine (June 13, 2024), BioVoice News (June 14, 2024)

claims.claim: The company reports established operational hubs across Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, with late 2024 expansions into parts of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
claims.source: Electronics For You (December 5, 2024), Startagist (November 29, 2024)
